objective: RC-D (rank 1 per DEC-20260805-f2086a, unrun since BATCH-010): a second, differently-constructed null object to test whether BATCH-009's OUTCOME-A (the r=5 excess did not survive substituting the cipher with a lazily-sampled IDEAL random permutation) depends on idealness specifically or on mere structurelessness more broadly (residual limitation U4, EV-AES-e4c091 unresolved_confounds). This batch builds a keyed PRP that is NOT an ideal oracle -- a fixed-round wide-block Feistel network with a round function built from arithmetic/mixing operations sharing no vocabulary with AES's S-box, MixColumns, or ShiftRows (the same independence bar rc8probe.c met against the yoyo_sbox_v2-v4 lineage) -- and reruns BATCH-009's matched-exposure comparison against it. UNLIKE the ideal-permutation oracle (which requires a pair-storage hash table, memory-bounded per BATCH-012's arithmetic ceiling), a directly-evaluated keyed Feistel PRP costs O(1) memory per query, so this instrument is not subject to the memory ceiling that bounds comparison B -- it should be able to reach a decisive exposure (order 2^30, matching BATCH-009's own N1 arm) within this batch's budget if the implementation is correct and the round count is chosen to keep per-query cost low.
budget_note: Declared 5400 s for the producer -- new instrument construction plus a real measurement run, not a recomputation. This is real engineering work (a keyed Feistel PRP implementation, an independence audit against the existing AES/yoyo_sbox/rc8probe vocabulary, and a preregistered comparison run), scoped smaller than BATCH-007's original rc8probe.c build (which also built the harness and ran the first two comparisons) because RC-D reuses rc8probe.c's existing plaintext-stream, oracle-harness, and matched-exposure comparison machinery -- only the oracle itself (perm128-style ideal permutation) is being swapped for a keyed Feistel PRP. 1200 s snapshot, 2400 s validation (larger than the producer step because independence-vocabulary and construction-correctness are the substantive checks a new oracle requires, mirroring BATCH-007's own validation budget). GOAL-AES-003 wall-clock ceilings are null by protocol-amendment-GOAL-AES-003-002.
batch_notes: THE SNAPSHOT-BEFORE-REVIEW SEQUENCING RULE MUST HOLD. Do not dispatch the reviewer before the snapshot archive is committed and dispatcher-verified, per BATCH-010's disclosed failure mode. THIS IS A NEW-INSTRUMENT BATCH, THE SAME SHAPE AS BATCH-007/BATCH-011: the round function's independence from AES's actual S-box/MixColumns/ShiftRows and from the yoyo_sbox_v2-v4 lineage must be demonstrated by direct code review, not asserted -- a keyed Feistel that reuses AES's S-box internally, even in a 'differently-constructed' wrapper, would not test idealness-vs-structurelessness at all, it would just be a smaller-round AES variant. THE INSTRUMENT MUST BE A KEYED PRP -- deterministic given the key, NOT resampled per trial like the perm128 ideal oracle -- since testing structuredness (a fixed algebraic map) versus idealness (a uniform random draw) is the entire point of this control; if the implementation resamples per trial it collapses back into another idealness test, not a structuredness test, and must be redesigned before any measurement run.

tasks.title: RC-D: build a keyed non-ideal Feistel PRP null object and rerun BATCH-009's matched-exposure comparison

handoff.objective: Build a fixed-round, keyed, deterministic Feistel-network PRP whose round function shares no vocabulary with AES's S-box/MixColumns/ShiftRows or the yoyo_sbox_v2-v4 lineage (verified by direct code audit, written into INDEPENDENCE_AUDIT.md before any measurement run), integrate it as a new oracle mode in a copy of rc8probe.c's existing harness (reusing the plaintext-stream and yoyo-statistic measurement machinery, NOT the perm128 ideal-permutation code), and rerun BATCH-009's matched-exposure comparison (same probe geometry, masks, r=5, matched exposure to BATCH-009's N1 arm at 2^30 trials if budget allows, otherwise the largest power-of-two exposure the budget supports, disclosed plainly) against this structured (non-ideal) null object instead of the ideal-permutation oracle.
handoff.uncertainty_reduced: Whether BATCH-009's OUTCOME-A (the r=5 excess vanishing under cipher substitution) depended on the substitute oracle being IDEAL specifically, or would also vanish under ANY sufficiently structureless/non-AES substitute -- including a deterministic, non-ideal, but still independently-constructed PRP. If the excess REAPPEARS under this structured substitute, that would suggest idealness itself (not mere non-AES-ness) is what removes the effect. If it STAYS ABSENT, that corroborates OUTCOME-A being robust to the substitute's specific construction.
inputs: ledger/evidence/EV-AES-e4c091.yaml (BATCH-009's OUTCOME-A, matched-exposure comparison methodology, preregistered decision rule)
ledger/evidence/EV-AES-acddd0.yaml (BATCH-011's rc8probe.c independence audit and harness -- reuse its plaintext-stream/measurement machinery, do not reuse its ideal-permutation oracle code)

src/rc8probe_feistel.c: the actual instrument. The Feistel round function must be built from operations that do not appear in AES's S-box, MixColumns, or ShiftRows definitions, and must not reuse any function, constant table, or code fragment from yoyo_sbox_v2.c/v3.c/v4.c or rc8probe's own perm128 ideal-permutation code. It must be a DETERMINISTIC KEYED MAP (same key -> same permutation across all trials), not resampled per trial -- resampling would make it another idealness test, not a structuredness test, and must be caught and corrected before running if found.

src/INDEPENDENCE_AUDIT.md: a direct side-by-side audit (not an assertion) demonstrating the round function's independence from AES's actual algebraic operations and from the yoyo_sbox_v2-v4/rc8probe-ideal codebase, in the same style and rigor as BATCH-011's rc8probe.c audit.

The matched-exposure comparison run(s) under runs/, at the SAME probe geometry (amask=1, smask=1), masks, and round count (r=5) as BATCH-009's N1 arm, at 2^30 trials if the budget and per-query cost allow it (report the actual measured per-query wall-clock cost and extrapolate honestly whether 2^30 is reachable BEFORE committing to that run size -- do not simply attempt 2^30 and let a timeout stand in for a measurement), otherwise the largest power-of-two exposure actually completed, disclosed plainly with the reason it stopped there.

RESULTS.json applying BATCH-009's own preregistered decision rule to this run's hit count against the matched live 5-round AES arm's reading (14 hits, cite the exact source), and stating plainly whether OUTCOME-A reappears (excess returns under a structured-but-non-ideal substitute) or stays absent (excess remains gone), with the honest caveat that a single run at a smaller exposure than BATCH-009's own has correspondingly less power, quantified explicitly.
